subject: Data Retention & Erasure Controls — SOC 2 artifacts request (FinSecure)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finsecure.example>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-02T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: Request: Evidence for retention/erasure controls for upcoming SOC 2 audit

Irene —

FinSecure's external auditor (ACME Audit) is running our annual SOC 2 next week and requested artefacts that show how Redwood enforces data retention and deletion for customer-scope data. Specifically they asked for:

- The current retention policy and any associated runbooks
- Evidence of scheduled deletion/erasure runs (timestamped logs) for at least one sample customer
- Configurations for region-based retention (EU) and any lifecycle rules (S3/GCS)
- Any supporting diagrams or dataflow that show where PII is persisted and how it's purged

Can you confirm what you can provide and a target ETA? Auditor would like materials in the next 7 business days. CC'ing Elena from ACME (auditor) on questions about formats.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Security Operations — FinSecure
liam.oconnor@finsecure.example

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the heads up and for looping ACME in. We can assemble a focused evidence packet for the auditor. To scope this efficiently: could you confirm whether ACME needs

1) A full system-level evidence set (policy + all logs + configs), or
2) A scoped customer sample (policy + runbook + deletion log for one customer) — which is often sufficient for the control objective testing?

What format does ACME prefer for logs (CSV vs JSON lines)? Also, do you need signed/hashed artifacts or is timestamped export acceptable?

We can provide the retention policy PDF, an internal runbook describing the erasure pipeline, lifecycle configuration snippets for the EU region, and a redacted timestamped deletion trace for a sample account. Estimated ETA for a curated packet is 72 hours once we have the preferred format and scope.

I'll coordinate with Soojin and Karthik on the artifacts.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Security Operations

Hi Liam / Irene —

Following up with the packet we discussed. I've attached a curated set (redacted where appropriate) and included short notes below each item:

- retention_policy_v3.pdf — current policy (effective 2025-06-01). Covers retention classes, retention-by-tag, and exceptions process.
- dataflow_delete_runbook.md — internal runbook for the erasure pipeline: scheduling, kube job names, fallback retries, and verification steps.
- erasure_log_sample.csv — sample output from a scheduled erasure job (columns: timestamp, object_id, customer_id_redacted, deletion_status, verification_hash). We exported as CSV per ACME's preference noted in past audits.
- s3_lifecycle_config.txt — snippet showing lifecycle rules for eu-west-1 bucket (transition + expiration rules).

Notes:
- We normally provide JSONL traces for engineering teams but can produce CSV for auditors (we included both styles in internal artifacts).
- The sample logs are redacted for customer IDs; we can provide an anonymized trace that preserves timestamps and object ids for control testing.

If ACME needs a signed manifest, we can include a signed hash file as well. Please let us know whether the CSV examples above are acceptable.

Regards,
Soojin Lee

Thanks, Soojin — this is a good start. A few follow-ups from ACME (Elena is copied):

- ACME would like to see a deletion trace that proves a full lifecycle: retention tag -> scheduled deletion -> verification (i.e., we want end-to-end proof the object was removed, not just job success codes). Is that achievable from your logs?
- For the EU scope, can you authoritatively confirm that deletion for EU-region accounts runs in-region and that any backups are subject to the same retention/erasure rules?
- Please provide a single anonymized but timestamped deletion trace for a sample customer (we do not need customer-identifying data). The auditor wants to correlate timestamps to job runs.

ACME's preferred formats: CSV for tabular logs, JSONL if you can produce a separate verification record. Also please upload artifacts to a shared, permissioned location (we can consume Drive links).

Target: material in the next 3 business days if possible.

Liam

Liam / Elena / team —

We can produce the end-to-end anonymized trace you described. Attached is an example anonymized JSONL trace (erasure_trace_20250904.jsonl) plus a CSV derived from the same run. The trace contains the following events (each line is one JSON object):

- tag_assigned: when the retention tag was applied to the object
- scheduled_deletion_created: scheduler entry created (job_id)
- deletion_attempted: storage API delete call with response code
- deletion_verified: verification step that checks absence from index and returns verification_hash

We confirm for EU-region buckets (eu-west-1) the erasure job runs on compute nodes colocated in the region and lifecycle rules are enforced for backups — snapshots older than retention period trigger the same erasure pipeline. Attached s3_lifecycle_config.txt shows the bucket rule and our backup retention note.

I've uploaded the anonymized packet to a permissioned Drive folder (link below) and included a signed manifest hash for tamper-evidence. If ACME would like a short walkthrough call, Marcus can join to show the runbook and live logs.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence

Let me know if you need anything else.
